calibre3d.title: Calibre3D
calibre3d.text: Calibre3D The Calibre3D profile is for the calibre3d project: a Python program that measures pieces with a RealSense camera. It is meant for people who have never used a terminal: choose the project's folder once, press one button, and everything it needs is installed. Using it Choose Calibre3D in the profile selector. Press Elegir carpeta and choose the folder of the calibre3d project (the one that holds the calibre3d package and requirements.txt ). It is remembered. Press Preparar entorno . The installation shows on the right, line by line. When it ends, the status turns Listo . No requirements.txt? If the project has no requirements.txt , the Entorno card says so. Descargar plantilla de requirements.txt writes one into the project folder with what calibre3d needs: Package Why numpy>=1.24 Point clouds and depth images. scipy>=1.10 Fitting the plane, segmenting and measuring the piece. matplotlib>=3.7 The thickness heat maps and the views (PNG). pyrealsense2>=2.55 The RealSense camera; Ver cámara and Guardar imagen need it too. It is the calibre3d project's own requirements.txt . The button never overwrites a file: if requirements.txt already exists, the template is saved beside it as requirements.plantilla.txt to compare. The status Status Means What to do 🔴 Sin proyecto No folder chosen, or it is gone. Press Elegir carpeta . 🔴 Sin entorno The folder has no .venv . Press Preparar entorno . 🟠 Incompleto .venv exists, but import calibre3d fails in it. Read the reason under the status (below). When the environment is incomplete, the card says why, from what Python answered: Reason shown Means En esta carpeta no está el programa calibre3d The folder chosen is not the one with the calibre3d package: choose the project's folder, the one with prueba.sh . Esta carpeta tiene prueba.sh pero le falta la carpeta calibre3d/ The right folder, but only prueba.sh was copied: copy the whole project, calibre3d/ included. Falta la librería X: añade Y a requirements.txt calibre3d imports a library that is not installed; Y is its pip name ( cv2 → opencv-python ). Error al cargar calibre3d: … Another error while importing; the text is Python's last line. 🟢 Listo import calibre3d works in .venv . The status is checked when the profile is first shown, when a folder is chosen, when an installation ends, and when you press Comprobar . It is not checked on every frame: the check starts Python once, which takes a moment. What "Preparar entorno" does In the project folder, one after the other, stopping at the first that fails: python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt Without a requirements.txt it only creates .venv and says there was nothing to install. An existing .venv is reused, not deleted. Pressing it again on a ready environment ( Volver a preparar ) installs whatever is missing. It needs python3 with the venv module and, for the dependencies, an internet connection. Calibrating and measuring Once the status is Listo , the Medir card runs calibre3d's steps in order, each with what to do before pressing it: Button Runs Do first 1. Plano python -m calibre3d plano Leave the mat empty. Once done, it says when and how noisy ("Hecho el 1 nov, 22:10 · ruido 0,04 mm"), from datos/plano.json . 2. Centrar python -m calibre3d centrar Put a coin on the cross. Its output says how far to move the mat; centrado_vista.png shows under it. 3. Medir python -m calibre3d medir <name> Put the piece inside the circle. It asks for the piece's name (letters, digits, - , _ ); a name already measured is refused, so no result is overwritten. Without a plane it says "Haz primero el plano", but lets you go on, as calibre3d does. Demo sin cámara python -m calibre3d demo Nothing: it measures a simulated piece, to try everything without the camera. While a step runs, its output shows live in Actividad and the other steps, the photo and the camera wait. The live camera is closed before each step (with a notice), since calibre3d needs the camera alone. When Medir or the demo ends well, the launcher reads the result file calibre3d left ( datos/resultados/<name>.json , or demo/resultados/demo_canto.json ) and shows a strip at the top of Actividad with the length, width, thickness and maximum Feret diameter, and calibre3d's warnings. It stays there, whatever runs next, until another measurement replaces it. Under the output come the heat map ( _mapa.png ) and the view ( _vista.png ). If a step fails, its error shows in red under Actividad and the last result stays as it was. patron (calibrating with pieces of known size) and plantilla (the mat's PDF) are not buttons yet: run them from a terminal in the project folder. Seeing the camera Once the status is Listo , Ver cámara in the Cámara card shows the camera live in the Actividad panel: the colour picture at 1280×720, about 15 frames a second, fitted to the panel in 16:9, with the camera's messages under it. Parar cámara closes it. The camera also closes by itself when you switch to another profile and when the window closes, so it is never left busy. While it is open the window redraws with every frame, which costs some processor; closed, the window goes back to sleeping until something happens. Behind it, preview.py (shipped inside the launcher, run with the project's .venv/bin/python ) writes each frame to its standard output as RSF1 , the width and height as big-endian 16-bit numbers, and the RGB bytes. The launcher keeps only the latest frame and paints it. Saving a photo Once the status is Listo , the Cámara card offers Guardar imagen : Press Guardar imagen . A dialog asks for the photo's name. Type a name (letters, digits, - and _ , no spaces, up to 64 characters) and press Guardar or Enter. A name already used is refused, so nothing is overwritten. With the camera open ( Ver cámara ), the photo is exactly the frame on screen, saved by the launcher without touching the camera. With it closed, the camera opens, skips 30 frames so its exposure settles, saves one colour frame at 1280×720 to datos/fotos/<name>.png inside the project, and closes again. The capture is a small Python script that ships inside the launcher ( internal/services/capture/capture.py ). It runs with the project's own .venv/bin/python and only needs pyrealsense2 , which requirements.txt installs; the PNG is written with Python's standard library. It does not depend on how the calibre3d package is written. Only one program can use the camera at a time: do not save a photo while another program has the camera open. Message Means No se encuentra ninguna RealSense conectada. No camera is connected, or it is not detected. No está instalado pyrealsense2 The environment lacks the camera library: press Preparar entorno . La cámara no responde The camera did not send frames for 5 seconds. La cámara aún está arrancando The live view has no frame yet: wait a moment and save again. Limits Listo means the package imports. It does not prove the camera is connected or that every dependency imported only later (inside a command) is installed. The photo capture, the live view and the steps that use the camera have only been tested against stand-ins for pyrealsense2 and calibre3d, not a real camera. The demo was run with the real calibre3d project.

get-started.title: Get started
get-started.text: Get started Build and run You need Go 1.25 or newer, a C compiler for cgo, and a display with OpenGL 4.1. go run ./cmd/script-launcher # follows the system's light or dark theme go run ./cmd/script-launcher -dark # forces the dark theme To keep it at hand, build a binary and put it in your PATH : go build -o ~/.local/bin/script-launcher ./cmd/script-launcher Add and run a script Press Añadir script . The picker opens in the folder of the last script you added. Choose a file. It is saved and selected. Press ▶ on its row. The output appears on the right and follows new lines until you scroll up. The script runs in its own folder, so relative paths inside it work as they do from a terminal opened there. Which program runs a file File Runs with .sh , .bash bash .py python3 .js , .mjs , .ts node anything else with the executable bit the file itself (its #! line decides) A file that matches none of these is refused when you add it. Where the list is kept In $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/script-launcher/ , which is ~/.config/script-launcher/ on most systems: File Holds scripts.json The saved scripts. settings.json The profile used last. -config-dir <folder> uses another folder. If either file is not valid JSON, the launcher refuses to start and says where it is, instead of overwriting it. Fix the file or delete it.

modules.title: Modules
modules.text: Modules The code is split in layers, each in its own folder under internal/ . Every layer only knows the ones below it, and cmd/script-launcher/main.go is the only place that builds them and passes each one what it needs. views ─→ profiles ─→ components ─→ session ─→ services ─→ domain └────→ data ─────→ domain Layer Files What it holds domain script.go , runner.go , output.go , profile.go Plain data and pure logic: a saved script, the runners and the registry that picks one, the output buffer, the profile IDs. No disk, no processes. data script_repository.go , settings_repository.go , their json_* implementations, json_file.go The repositories and their JSON files. The disk sits behind a FileStore , so tests use a map. services run_service.go , run.go , python_env_service.go , capture_service.go , preview_service.go Starting, watching and stopping processes; one Run per execution, safe to read from the UI while its goroutines write. Preparing and checking a Python .venv , saving photos, and the live camera view, with the scripts embedded in capture/ . views/session session.go , actions.go What every profile shares: the scripts, the selection, the notices, the file picker, and the actions (add, remove, run, stop). views/components script_list.go , output_panel.go , bar.go , … The pieces layouts are built from. Each draws from a session and calls its actions. views/profiles profile.go , default.go , calibre3d*.go The layouts, and the registry the selector offers. Calibre3D is split by card: project, environment, camera. views app_view.go The window: toolbar with the profile selector, the active profile, status bar, picker, notices. A frame Go UI is immediate mode: there are no widget objects. Each frame AppView.Draw draws the toolbar, then calls the active profile's Draw with the session, then the status bar. A run's goroutines call window.Wake() after every line, so the window draws only when something changed and sleeps otherwise. Adding a profile A profile is anything that implements profiles.Profile : type Profile interface { ID() domain.ProfileID Name() string Draw(context *ui.Context, current *session.Session) } Add its ID to internal/domain/profile.go . Write the layout in a new file in internal/views/profiles/ , building it from components ( ScriptList , ScriptRow , RunButtons , OutputPanel , OutputLines , Bar ) and plain Go UI. Add it to DefaultRegistry in profile.go . The selector shows profiles in that order; the first one is used when the saved profile is unknown. A profile that needs state of its own (a chosen tab, a typed value) keeps it in its own struct fields and is registered as a pointer. One that needs services gets them in a constructor, called from main.go , as NewCalibre3D(env, settings) does. Adding a kind of script A runner is anything that implements domain.Runner : type Runner interface { ID() string Matches(path string, executable bool) bool Command(path string) (program string, args []string) } For a new interpreter, add an InterpreterRunner to DefaultRegistry in internal/domain/runner.go , before the ExecutableRunner fallback: InterpreterRunner{Program: "ruby", Extensions: []string{".rb"}}, Then add a case to TestResolvesInterpreterByExtension . Tests go test -race ./... domain and data are tested with plain values and an in-memory FileStore . services runs the small scripts in internal/services/testdata , creates real .venv s, and saves photos through a stand-in pyrealsense2 ( testdata/fake_realsense ) that returns a solid frame, checking the PNG it writes. views opens the window headless with Go UI's uitest , clicks the real buttons and the profile selector by name, and checks what the window shows.

overview.title: Overview

sections.text: What it does not do yet

overview.text: Overview Script Launcher is a desktop window that keeps a list of your scripts and runs them with one click. You find a script on disk once; after that it is a row in the list, ready to run. The interface is in Spanish; the names below are the ones on its buttons. What it does Añadir script opens a file picker. The chosen file is checked (it must exist and be something the launcher knows how to run) and saved to the list. ▶ runs the script. Its standard output and error appear live on the right, errors in red. ■ stops it: the launcher sends SIGTERM to the script and every process it started. When the script ends, the last line says how: its exit code and how long it took. The row shows a green tick, a red cross or a grey square. 🗑 removes a script from the list. The file on disk is left alone. A script whose file was moved or deleted shows a warning sign and cannot be run. The profile selector in the toolbar changes the window's layout. General is the list of scripts beside their output; Calibre3D prepares the calibre3d project's environment in one click ( Calibre3D ). Every profile shares the same list, running scripts keep running when you switch, and the window opens on the profile used last. What it does not do yet Pass arguments or environment variables to a script. Read from the keyboard: a script's standard input is empty, so a script that asks a question gets no answer. Keep the output of past runs after the window closes. See the roadmap .

primera-instalacion.text: Primera instalación (macOS y Fedora) Esta guía es para dejar listo un ordenador recién sacado de la caja: instalar lo necesario, conectar la cámara RealSense D405 y hacer la primera medida con Script Launcher. No hace falta saber programar. Donde haya que escribir algo en la terminal, cópialo y pégalo tal cual. Sigue solo los pasos de tu sistema: macOS (un Mac) o Fedora (Linux). Qué necesitas El ordenador, con conexión a internet. La cámara Intel RealSense D405 y su cable USB-C. Conéctala directamente al ordenador, sin hubs ni alargadores. La carpeta del proyecto calibre3d (te la pasarán en un USB o en una descarga). Es la carpeta que contiene prueba.sh , requirements.txt y otra carpeta llamada calibre3d . El tapete impreso y la cámara montada a unos 133 mm sobre él (lo explica el README.md del proyecto). 1. Instalar Python Script Launcher usa Python para hablar con la cámara y hacer las medidas. macOS Entra en python.org/downloads y pulsa el botón amarillo Download Python 3.x . Abre el archivo descargado ( python-3.x-macos11.pkg ) y pulsa Continuar hasta el final. Al terminar se abre una carpeta de Python: haz doble clic en Install Certificates.command . Se abre una ventana negra; cuando diga que ha terminado, ciérrala. No uses el Python que el Mac ofrece instalar con las «herramientas de desarrollo»: Script Launcher busca primero el de python.org. Fedora Ya viene instalado. No hay que hacer nada. 2. Dar permiso para usar la cámara Fedora Linux no deja usar la cámara a un usuario normal hasta que se le dice que es de confianza. Abre la aplicación Terminal (búscala en el menú), pega estas tres líneas y pulsa Intro. Te pedirá tu contraseña: sudo curl -L -o /etc/udev/rules.d/99-realsense-libusb.rules https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IntelRealSense/librealsense/master/config/99-realsense-libusb.rules sudo udevadm control --reload-rules sudo udevadm trigger Después desconecta la cámara y vuelve a conectarla . macOS No hay que instalar nada. Si al ver la cámara aparece un error de permisos USB, mira Si algo falla . 3. Descargar Script Launcher Entra en la página de descargas: github.com/Itros97/script-launcher/releases/latest macOS Descarga ScriptLauncher-macOS.zip . Sirve para todos los Mac (M1–M4 e Intel). Abre el zip: aparece Script Launcher . Arrástralo a la carpeta Aplicaciones . La primera vez, el Mac dirá que no puede comprobar el desarrollador. Es normal: la app no está firmada con una cuenta de pago de Apple. Para abrirla: Abre Ajustes del Sistema → Privacidad y seguridad . Baja hasta el aviso sobre «Script Launcher» y pulsa Abrir igualmente . Confirma con Abrir . Solo hay que hacerlo una vez. Fedora Descarga script-launcher-linux-x86_64.tar.gz . Abre la carpeta Descargas, haz clic derecho en el archivo y elige Extraer aquí . Abre la Terminal y pega: bash ~/Descargas/script-launcher-linux-x86_64/install.sh Si tu sistema está en inglés, la carpeta se llama Downloads en vez de Descargas . Script Launcher ya aparece en el menú de aplicaciones. 4. Poner el proyecto calibre3d en su sitio Copia la carpeta calibre3d a tu carpeta Documentos (en Fedora, Documentos ; en Mac, Documentos también). Así no se pierde entre las descargas. Dentro de esa carpeta deben verse, al menos, prueba.sh , requirements.txt y otra carpeta calibre3d . 5. Preparar Calibre3D en Script Launcher Abre Script Launcher . Arriba a la izquierda, en el desplegable, elige Calibre3D . En la tarjeta Proyecto , pulsa Elegir carpeta . Se abre un selector (sus botones están en inglés): pulsa Home a la izquierda, haz clic en Documentos y luego en calibre3d (la de fuera, la que tiene prueba.sh ) para entrar en ella, y pulsa Choose . En la tarjeta Entorno , pulsa Preparar entorno . A la derecha verás cómo se instala todo. Tarda unos minutos y descarga unos 300 MB. Cuando termine, el entorno dice 🟢 Listo . 6. Comprobar que todo funciona En la tarjeta Medir , pulsa Demo sin cámara . En unos segundos aparecen arriba las medidas de una pieza simulada (unos 60 × 40 × 20 mm) y, debajo, su mapa de calor. Si lo ves, el programa funciona. Con la D405 conectada, en la tarjeta Cámara pulsa Ver cámara . A la derecha debe verse lo que ve la cámara. Pulsa Parar cámara cuando acabes. 7. Medir una pieza Calienta la cámara unos 10 minutos antes de empezar: la medida cambia un poco con la temperatura. 1. Plano : deja el tapete vacío y pulsa el botón. Se hace una vez al empezar la sesión. 2. Centrar : pon una moneda sobre la cruz del tapete y pulsa. A la derecha dice cuánto mover el tapete; muévelo y repite hasta que diga «Centrado». 3. Medir : pon la pieza dentro del círculo, pulsa, escribe un nombre (por ejemplo muestra_001 , sin espacios) y pulsa Guardar . Arriba aparecen el largo, el ancho, el espesor y el Feret; debajo, el mapa de calor. Todo se guarda en la carpeta del proyecto, en datos/resultados/ . Las fotos de Guardar imagen van a datos/fotos/ . Si algo falla Lo que ves Qué hacer «No encuentro python3» En Mac, instala Python desde python.org (paso 1) y vuelve a abrir Script Launcher. «Sin proyecto» o «En esta carpeta no está el programa calibre3d» Pulsa Elegir carpeta , entra en la carpeta calibre3d de fuera (la que tiene prueba.sh ) y pulsa Choose . «Esta carpeta tiene prueba.sh pero le falta la carpeta calibre3d/» Falta parte del proyecto: vuelve a copiar la carpeta completa. «Incompleto» con «Falta la librería…» Pulsa Preparar entorno otra vez. Si se repite, añade la librería que dice a requirements.txt . La instalación falla con errores de red Comprueba la conexión a internet y pulsa Preparar entorno otra vez. «No se encuentra ninguna RealSense conectada» Conecta la cámara directamente al ordenador, sin hub. En Fedora, repite el paso 2 y reconecta la cámara. En Mac, un error de permisos USB al usar la cámara Por verificar en un Mac: en algunas versiones de macOS la librería de la cámara necesita permisos de administrador. Avisa a quien te pasó el programa. En Mac, la instalación dice que no encuentra pyrealsense2 Por verificar en un Mac: puede que tu versión de Python aún no tenga la librería de la cámara. Avisa a quien te pasó el programa con el texto rojo de la derecha. La medida da avisos en naranja («Pieza lejos del centro»…) Lee el aviso: suele bastar con centrar la pieza o repetir el plano. Nota: la parte de macOS no se ha probado todavía en un Mac con la D405. Si algo no coincide con lo que ves, apúntalo y pásalo para corregir la guía.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.text: Roadmap Ideas, roughly in order. None of them is promised. Calibre3D patterns and mat : buttons for patron <name> --real L A E and plantilla . Calibre3D history : the list of past measurements, to open one again, and export them as CSV. Calibre3D camera : the depth image beside the colour one, guides drawn over the live view (the cross and the circle), and a thumbnail of the last photo. Arguments per script : a field on each script for arguments, saved with it. Environment variables per script, read from an ignored .env file next to it. Rename and reorder the saved scripts, and group them in folders. Run history : keep the last few runs of each script, with their output, after the window closes. Standard input : a field under the output to type answers to a script that asks. Notifications when a long script ends while the window is in the background. Copy output to the clipboard, and a search over it. A monospaced font for the output, once Go UI offers one.
